subject: Post-call recap: pricing, token volumes & rate limits
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: pricing, token volumes & rate limits

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery call:

- Estimated usage: 50–200M tokens/month in pilot, scaling to ~1B tokens/month over 12 months depending on feature rollout.
- Budget: you mentioned a target procurement range of $15k–$60k/month initially; you said target unit economics of ~$18 per 1M tokens as a stretch goal for large volume.
- Questions you had: burst usage behavior, quota increases, and overage pricing/terms.

Attaching our latest pricing sheet (pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) and the traffic export you mentioned (traffic_patterns_q1.csv) to make it easier for you to model costs. Short answers below and happy to dive deeper on a follow-up:

Unit economics & pricing (high level):
- Hosted API list: $25 / 1M tokens (pay-as-you-go)
- Volume discounts: 5% at 50M/mo, 20% at 500M/mo, custom committed pricing (can approach $18 / 1M) for 1B+ tokens with a 12-mo commit.

Rate limits & overage:
- Burst allowance: customers get a standard burst of up to +20% above their daily quota for short spikes; sustained excess beyond burst will be throttled.
- Quota increases: request via account manager/support; standard turnaround 48 hours for hosted customers, faster for Dedicated.
- Overage pricing: overage billed at 120% of the committed unit price for the billing period unless a temporary quota increase is approved ahead of time.

Next steps:
1) Would you confirm the most likely pilot monthly token range (low/expected/high) so we can run a cost model for both pay-as-you-go and a 12-mo committed scenario?
2) If $18 / 1M tokens is the target, can you share the anticipated monthly floor (e.g., >=500M tokens) to make that pricing viable?
3) I'll schedule a follow-up next week with Marissa (solutions) to map workload characteristics that affect batching/kv-cache savings.

Available times: Tue 3/2 10–11am PT, Wed 3/3 9–11am PT. Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, traffic_patterns_q1.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@acmeretail.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing, token volumes & rate limits

Thanks Camila — very helpful summary.

Couple of follow-ups from my side:
- Pilot expected tokens: 40M low / 120M expected / 350M high per month (features ramp over 3 months).
- Our procurement team is pushing for a target of $18 / 1M tokens for committed pricing. Is $18 attainable at ~1B annualized volume or do we need to commit to higher minimums?
- Burst patterns: we have weekday spikes during marketing campaigns that can be 2–3x baseline for 1–2 hours. How does Redwood handle short high-amplitude spikes? Is the +20% burst enough, or do you offer higher temporary allowances?
- Overage: can you clarify whether overage is billed monthly or pro-rated daily, and whether there's a cap we can negotiate for enterprise customers?

I've attached the traffic export on our side (traffic_patterns_q1.csv) with an example spike day.

Can we lock the follow-up for Wed 3/3 10am PT? Also please share the pricing sheet and any example cost models for pay-as-you-go vs committed at the ranges above.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake | Head of Product, Acme Retail
jordan@acmeretail.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing, token volumes & rate limits

Jordan — great data, thanks for the file. Quick responses inline:

- $18 / 1M tokens: Achievable with a committed pricing agreement. Typical approach: 12-mo commit at ~1B tokens/year (average ~83M/mo) or higher. For calendarized monthly commitments, we can structure a stepped discount so you hit ~$18 / 1M at ~1B+ annual run-rate. I’ll have Marissa pull an example model and share.

- Burst handling: Our hosted customers get a default burst allowance of +20% over daily quota to handle brief spikes. For your described 2–3x hour-long spikes, +20% won't be sufficient. Options:
  1) Temporary quota increase (approved by account manager) — we can pre-authorize an elevated daily burst for campaign windows (turnaround 24–48 hours).
  2) Short-term committed buffer — we can include a short-term elevated quota for N days as part of the contract (good for planned campaigns).
  3) Dedicated/Dedicated-like routing for extremely bursty patterns (recommended for sustained 2–3x patterns) — gives more predictable throttling and capacity.

- Overage billing: Overage is billed monthly and is measured against committed monthly quota. Standard term: overage invoiced at 120% of the committed unit price unless we agree on a negotiated cap. For enterprise deals we can negotiate an overage cap (e.g., no more than 150% of committed spend in any month) as part of the SOW; this requires legal/finance approval.

- Pro-rating: We do not pro-rate down to the day for committed quotas; increases are effective from the approval date and billed in the next cycle. However temporary increases for campaign windows can be made retroactive if pre-approved by the AM.

I'll attach a simple cost model comparing:
- Pay-as-you-go at list ($25/1M) with no commit
- 12-mo commit models that show effective $/1M at 250M, 500M, 1B tokens/month

Next steps:
- Marissa will prepare the committed vs PAYG model by EOD Mon and I’ll schedule Wed 3/3 10am PT.
- Do you want us to draft a preliminary MA (MA_draft.docx) with the target pricing anchors so procurement can review?

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Camila

Attachments: MA_draft.docx, pricing_sheet_v2.pdf
